transcript.content: Hello, I'm Dr. Smith. It's nice to meet you; what brings you in to see me today?

Hi, Dr. Smith. It's really nice to meet you too. Thank you so much for fitting me in. 

Um... I guess what finally pushed me to come in is that... well, my eating has just been a little all over the place lately. I hope that's an okay thing to start with. It's probably not a huge deal, but some weeks I barely touch my dinner. I just don't feel like having anything. But then... other nights, I find myself just standing in the kitchen eating crackers and sweets after everyone else has gone to bed. 

It's a bit embarrassing to admit, honestly. I know a lot of people go through weird phases with food, right? It just felt like maybe I should finally talk to someone about it, if that makes sense.
During those nights when you find yourself eating crackers and sweets, do you feel like you are unable to stop or control how much you are eating?

Oh, no, no... I wouldn't say I can't stop. It's really not like that. Um, I definitely have control over it. It's not like I'm emptying the whole pantry or doing anything crazy. 

I just... I guess I just get a little snacky? Like I'll have a few crackers and think, well, maybe just one more, or a little piece of chocolate. But I can stop whenever I want to. I hope I didn't make it sound worse than it actually is. It's really just normal late-night snacking, I think. A lot of people do that, don't they?
Outside of these moments with food, have you been feeling down, depressed, or hopeless for most of the day, nearly every day, for the past couple of weeks?

Oh, um... well, I wouldn't say hopeless. That sounds a bit too strong, doesn't it? I really try to stay positive. But... I guess I do go through these stretches sometimes. 

It’s hard to explain... it's just that sometimes the house feels sort of gray and heavy. And I’ll find myself just sitting at the kitchen table, feeling a little empty, even though absolutely nothing terrible has happened that day. 

I know it sounds silly when I say it out loud. Everyone gets the blues occasionally, right? I really hope I don't sound like I'm just complaining... is that the kind of thing you were asking about?
How long have you been feeling this way—has it been going on for most days over the last few weeks, or would you say this has been a more persistent feeling for months or even years?

Oh, um... well, it definitely hasn't been years or anything like that! I don't want you to think I've just been sitting around feeling sorry for myself forever. I really do try to push through it and keep busy. 

But... I guess if I look back and sort of add up all those gray periods... you know, the times where I just lose interest in my usual things and feel kind of guilty for no good reason... I suppose it's added up to about seven months? Give or take? 

I hope I'm answering your question the right way. It's just that it comes and goes, so it's hard to measure exactly. Is seven months a really long time to feel like this? I really hope I haven't let it go on for too long before coming in to talk to you...
During those 'gray' periods you mentioned, do you experience a significant change in your sleep patterns, such as sleeping much more or much less than usual?

Oh, no, my sleep is... it's pretty normal, I think. I mean, I definitely don't sleep the day away or anything like that. I try really hard to keep a regular schedule, you know? 

I guess sometimes when I'm feeling a little down, it might take me a few extra minutes to get out of bed in the morning, but I always get up. And at night, I usually just go to sleep at my normal time. I really don't think there's any big change there. I hope that's okay? I just try to make sure I get a good night's rest so I can be productive the next day.
When you are going through these 'gray' periods, do you often find yourself feeling inadequate or like you are not as capable as the people around you?

Oh, um... well, I wouldn't say inadequate, exactly. I mean, I know I'm capable of doing things, and I really try my best to be a good partner and everything. I don't want you to think I just sit around feeling useless. 

But... I guess sometimes when things feel heavy, I do get a little... stuck? Like, I'll spend hours just replaying these tiny little things in my head. Like, maybe I bought a slightly more expensive tube of paint than I needed to, or maybe I was a little short with my husband when he asked me a question. 

And then I just... I start to feel so bad about it. Like I've somehow ruined the whole household just by doing that one little thing. I know it sounds completely out of proportion when I say it like that. I really try not to let it get to me, but it just kind of spirals sometimes. Is that... is that the sort of thing you mean? I hope I'm not making a big deal out of nothing...
When you are going through these periods, do you find yourself feeling generally low about your self-worth or like you are just not as good as other people?

Oh, um... yeah, I guess it really ties into what I was just saying a moment ago. I'm sorry if I'm repeating myself! I don't necessarily walk around thinking I'm completely worthless compared to everyone else... I really do try to keep my chin up and be positive. 

But... when I get stuck replaying those little things, like I mentioned with the expensive pigment or being short with my husband... that's when it hits me. I just get this overwhelming feeling that I've ruined the whole household because of my mistakes. It's more of this huge, heavy guilt over those tiny little slip-ups rather than thinking I'm a bad person overall. 

I know it sounds so silly to get that worked up over a tube of paint, and I really try to snap myself out of it. Am I making sense? I just want to make sure I'm giving you the right information and answering what you actually meant.
During these periods when you are feeling low, do you find that you have less energy than you usually do, or that you feel physically tired more often?

Oh, um... no, I wouldn't say that. I really try to make sure I keep moving, you know? I don't want you to think I'm the type of person who just sits around on the couch all day just because I'm having a rough patch. 

I think it's really important to keep up with things around the house, so... physically, my energy is pretty normal. I still do all my chores and take care of what I need to do. I really push myself to stay active because I know that's what you're supposed to do to stay healthy. 

I hope that's okay? I just... I definitely don't feel physically drained or anything like that. I try to be really good about staying productive, even when my mood is a little off.
During these periods when your mood is low, do you find that you have lost interest in or no longer get pleasure from the hobbies or activities that you usually enjoy?

Oh, um... well, I really try to stay engaged, I promise I do. I know how important it is to keep up with your hobbies and stay social. I don't want to sound like I just give up on everything. 

But... I guess, if I'm being completely honest, sometimes when I'm in one of those low spells... things I usually really look forward to just kind of feel... different? Like, I normally love going to my book club, or trying new recipes, or going to art galleries... and I take a lot of pride in tending my rose beds. I really do. 

But during those times, they just sort of start to feel like... chores? Like things I just keep putting off instead of wanting to do them. I still try to force myself to do them because I know I should, but the spark just isn't quite there. 

Does that make sense? I hope that doesn't make me sound lazy or ungrateful for the nice things in my life. I really do try my best to stay interested in things...
Aside from these low periods, have you ever experienced times where you felt unusually energetic, talkative, or productive, to the point where you felt like you didn't need much sleep?

Oh, um... well, I wouldn't say I'm ever out of control or anything like that. I really try to channel my energy into good things, you know? Being productive and helpful around the house. I don't want you to think I'm running around acting crazy.

But... yes, sometimes I do get these bursts where I just feel so... capable? Like I can get everything done. And during those times, I guess I really don't need a lot of rest. I can sleep maybe three or four hours and wake up feeling completely charged. 

I actually get a lot done! I'll be up ready to write blog posts or plan out all these new projects before the sun is even up. I always make sure I'm quiet so I don't wake my husband, though. I try to be very considerate about it. 

Is it okay to have energy like that sometimes? I just figured it was a good thing to be so productive, but I hope it doesn't sound like I'm doing something wrong...
During these periods when you feel so capable and only need three or four hours of sleep, do you find that your thoughts are racing, or that you are talking much faster than usual?

Oh, um... well, I really try to communicate clearly, I promise I do. I don't want to be difficult to understand or seem scattered. I always try to think before I speak so I make sense to people. 

But... I suppose, when I have all that energy... my mind just gets so full of wonderful ideas. It's like everything is connected, and my thoughts just run so, so fast. One idea just bumps right into the next—like, I'll be thinking about my roses, and then how much money we need for the garden, and then the colors of the petals, and then secret messages in the colors, and then maybe taking a horticulture class... 

It's all very exciting, but sometimes I just can't slow my brain down quite enough to explain it all to my husband before the next thought comes. I might talk a little faster just trying to get it all out before I lose it. 

I hope that doesn't make me sound frantic or anything? I just get so inspired, and I want to share it all. I really do try to pace myself when I talk to people, though. Is it normal to get a little ahead of yourself when you're feeling that good?

During these periods when you feel so energetic and your thoughts are racing, have you ever felt that your behavior was so different or intense that it caused noticeable problems for you at work, with your husband, or in your social life?

Oh, um... well, I really try hard not to let things get out of hand. I always want to be responsible and stay on top of my tasks, I promise I do. I don't want you to think my life is just falling apart or that I'm ignoring my duties. 

But... I suppose, if I'm looking at it honestly... it does get a little tricky sometimes. I don't like admitting it, but I've actually sort of... fallen behind on my facilitator training recently. And my private blog work, too. It's just that, with so many ideas coming at once, my projects and all my explanations just became really hard to organize. I kept trying to make sense of them for everyone else, but things just got a bit tangled up.

And with my husband... well, he's wonderful, but there has been a little bit of tension at home because of it all. It just makes it harder to keep up with our normal routines together when I'm running on such a different wavelength. I always apologize and try to make it right, though. 

I hope that doesn't make me sound like a bad wife, or like I'm not trying hard enough to keep my life together. I really am trying my best to manage it all. Is it understandable that I struggle with my routine a little bit when my mind gets like that?

Have you ever had a period of time, lasting at least a full week, where your energy and racing thoughts were so intense that you required hospitalization or were unable to function in your daily life at all?

Oh, um... no, definitely not. I really make sure I never let things get that far. I would never want to be a burden on anyone or have to go to the hospital. I know that sounds terrible, and I always try to keep myself grounded before anything like that could happen. 

I mean, even when I have all that energy and my thoughts are moving quickly, I'm still here at home, trying to keep up with things. I might get a little disorganized, like I mentioned with my blog and my training, but I'm definitely not completely unable to function. I'm still trying my best to do my part. 

I've never had to be hospitalized for feeling too energetic. That would mean I was really out of control, right? I promise I always try to stay on top of myself so I don't cause any major problems. I hope that's the right answer? I just want you to know I really do try to be responsible.
When you have these periods of high energy and racing thoughts, do they typically last for at least four days in a row?

Oh, um... yes, they definitely last that long. I hope that's okay to admit. I don't want you to think I'm just constantly wound up, because I really do try to stay calm and collected as much as I can. 

But... well, if I'm being completely honest, these stretches where I'm just so energized and, you know, maybe taking on a bit too much... they've actually been happening for quite a while now. I'd say it's been about a year and eight months that these periods have been a part of my life. 

They definitely stick around for at least four days, usually longer, just humming along in the background. I really try to channel it into good things, like my projects, so I'm not just wasting it. I hope it doesn't make me sound like I've been unstable for a long time? I just try to make the best of it when it happens. Is it common for people to have these energetic phases off and on for that long?
